title: Sable and Lotus: a 10th-century East Asian tactics RPG built in Unity with coding agents, code-drawn pixel art, and AI portraits/music
author: ignitesplash123
selftext:
>Hey everyone! I’ve been working on an indie game called *Sable and Lotus*, and I wanted to share a bit about it.  
>  
>I love history, and I wanted to explore a time and place we don’t see much in games. So I ended up in 10th-century East Asia, following a scribe who finds herself in a Khitan prince’s camp.  
>  
>She doesn’t fight herself. Instead, you help run the prince’s travelling household and give orders during battles using a signal drum. I’ve always loved the big battles in Total War, RPG stories and characters, and base-building games, so I’ve been trying to bring some of those ideas together. The manga *Jaduugar* was an inspiration too.  
>  
>I’m also writing a light novel and making a manga set in the same world. Chapter 1 of the game is almost ready. It isn’t available publicly yet, but I’m planning to bring it to Steam.  
>  
>For development, I’ve been using Claude Code, Codex and Gemini together. One thing I learned is that AI-generated images weren’t giving me the consistency I wanted for small sprites. So I had coding agents help me build a pixel-art toolkit and draw the field sprites in code. That way I can rebuild them consistently as the game changes. I still use generative tools for character portraits and music.  
>  
>I’m curious how other people keep small 2D sprites consistent, or keep multiple coding agents working together without getting in each other’s way.  
>  
>The site has a trailer and screenshots if you’d like to see it: [https://sable-and-lotus-game.pages.dev/](https://sable-and-lotus-game.pages.dev/)  
>  
>Happy to answer any questions about the project!

comments.author: No_Rock5928
comments.body: hi How did you do background assets and Environment assets?

replies.author: ignitesplash123
replies.body:
Hey! For the in-game environments, I'm using a similar approach to the character sprites. I have Claude Code and Codex help write pixel-art generation code.

Buildings, tents, terrain tiles, trees, and other environmental elements are also drawn programmatically and assembled in Unity.
